subject: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:15:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Elena / Julian —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Wanted to capture a concise recap of the pain points, success criteria, and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned. If I missed anything, say so and I’ll update.

Key pain points you shared
- Unit economics: inference spend has become the single largest line item in your ML infra budget (forecasted to double next quarter).
- Bursty traffic for fraud detections + high-volume nightly batch jobs for embeddings — current infra is expensive and underutilized outside peaks.
- Latency sensitivity: customer-facing scoring paths need p95 <200ms; internal batch jobs can tolerate higher latency.
- Quality constraints: past quantization attempts introduced unacceptable regressions for high-sensitivity signals.

Current stack (high level)
- Models: mix of open LLMs for embeddings and a few in-house fine-tuned classifiers.
- Hosting: self-hosted endpoints on AWS (p3/p4 family) + some traffic routed through a commercial LLM API for peak overflow.
- Observability: basic Prometheus metrics + application logs, but limited token-level cost attribution.

Success criteria you called out
- Reduce per-token/unit inference cost by ~30% (primary goal).
- Maintain or improve p95 latency on customer-facing paths (<200ms target).
- No regression on critical quality metrics (false-positive rate for fraud models).
- Security/compliance: SOC2 summary and audit evidence needed for procurement.

What we discussed re: technical levers
- Batching & caching: prefix/KV caching for chat-like flows and smart batching for high-throughput batch jobs — you're open to batching for batch jobs but want strict latency budgets for real-time scoring.
- Quantization: willing to experiment with int8/quantized variants on non-customer-facing models; conservative approach for models used in high-sensitivity paths.
- Model routing: interested in cost-tiered routing (cheaper variants for non-critical traffic; fallback to higher-quality models when needed).

Attachments I’m including
- mutual-action-plan.pdf (stub M A P with timeline & owners)
- fintechcorp-inference-metrics.csv (sample token/latency distribution you volunteered during the call)

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive (90 mins): Marissa to lead. We’ll walk through your token distribution, latency SLOs, and test dataset for quality checks. Please share any additional sample traffic or model artifacts before the call.
2) Redwood will produce a high-level sizing + cost-reduction plan (inc. rough unit economics) within 5 business days after the deep-dive.
3) Security & procurement: I’ve attached our SOC2 summary and can introduce our compliance lead if you need anything for procurement.
4) Pilot: small PoC targeting your nightly embedding pipeline (lower-risk) to validate batching/caching and quantization benefits.

Proposed times for the technical deep-dive (PST): Tue 12/1 10:00–11:30, Tue 12/1 14:00–15:30, Wed 12/2 09:00–10:30 — let me know what works.

Thanks again — really excited to see how much we can move the needle on unit economics while keeping your critical paths stable.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182

---
Attachment stubs included: mutual-action-plan.pdf (2 pages), fintechcorp-inference-metrics.csv (sample, 1.2MB)
From: Elena Rossi <elena@fintechcorp.com>

Cc: Julian Park <julian@fintechcorp.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — inference cost pressure & next steps

Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. This aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications and asks from our side:

1) Procurement timeline: we’re budgeting for a Q1 deployment decision; procurement/contract review will take ~6 weeks once we have an initial SOW/pricing.
2) Pricing: can you provide a ballpark (non-binding) pricing delta for a pilot that targets ~20M tokens/month? We understand it’s rough but want to model it into our forecasts.
3) Model fallback: is it simple to route certain traffic to a higher-cost variant on failure/low-confidence? We want automated fallbacks to preserve quality.
4) Security: please share SOC2 summary and any documentation on data retention and customer-managed keys.

Julian (cc) will own procurement questions. We’ll confirm a time for the technical deep-dive — Tue 12/1 14:00–15:30 PST looks good from our side.

Elena Rossi
Head of ML Infrastructure
FinTechCorp
elena@fintechcorp.com | +1 212-555-0199
